parole.testo: From Middle French gaufre, from Old French walfre, from Frankish *wāfilu, *wāfilā or Middle Dutch wafele, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *wēbilǭ, *wēbilō, possibly related to Proto-Indo-European *webʰ- (“to braid, weave”). Cognate with English waffle. Related also to German Wabe (“honeycomb”).
